title: Regional Fanout Probability Editor & Policy Playbook
creator: Ava Morales
description: Goal: Ship a Console-first, customer-configurable policy editor that lets platform engineers and product teams compose region/tier routing with probabilistic fanout and explicit fallback model variants. This ticket scopes the UX surface, validation rules, preview/simulator experience, and handoff acceptance criteria for eng and design. Motivations: customers need fine-grained controls to split traffic across regions and Dedicated tiers for cost/latency tradeoffs, while ensuring robust fallbacks when preferred capacity is unavailable. The editor should support weight-based distribution, probability sliders, deterministic overrides for keys (region pinning), and automated suggestions for compatible fallback model variants. It should also integrate live validation that prevents contradictory rules and surface a cost/latency delta preview for the composed policy.
acceptance_criteria: UI: New 'Fanout' tile in Policy Editor where user can add multiple regions and tiers and assign weight or probability to each target
Validation: Console warns and blocks save when rules are mutually exclusive or total weight != 100% unless explicitly marked as probabilistic
Preview: Simulator can run a dry-run with synthetic traffic to show per-region expected RPS, mean latency, and estimated cost delta compared to a single-region baseline
Fallbacks: UX enables selecting fallback model variants per-target with auto-suggested compatible variants and an explanation for compatibility (quantization, architecture, latency tier)
Export: Policy can be exported to JSON policy-as-code format and validated against the runtime schema used by Smart Router
Telemetry hooks: Policy page links to existing route-level telemetry and shows expected telemetry tags for each target (e.g., region, tier, model_variant)
E2E: ENG acceptance tests verify policy change flows through control plane to runtime and triggers expected routing behavior in a staged environment
design_notes: Primary workflow: create policy -> add fanout targets -> set weights/probabilities -> assign fallbacks -> run preview -> save/publish
Probability slider with numeric input, and an optional toggle to convert to deterministic round-robin for sticky keys
Compact matrix view for large customers with >8 regions: allow collapsing tiers into groups and applying group-level weights
Inline explanations and links to learn more about cost estimation and model compatibility
Accessibility: keyboard-first controls for slider and matrix; high-contrast delineation for active fallback targets
tradeoffs_and_decisions: We considered building a full DSL editor but chose a guided visual composer to reduce user error and support PLG adoption
Cost preview is an expected-value estimate (not a guarantee); accuracy depends on recent telemetry; will include a confidence band
Automatic fallback suggestions are conservative: only suggest variants tested in our compatibility matrix to avoid behavioral regressions
Simulation runs in the browser for small synthetic loads; larger simulations will call a sandbox service (ENG-72415) to run cluster-level projections
risks: Customers may misconfigure probabilistic rules leading to unexpected costs; mitigated with stronger warnings and a required 'are you sure' for cost delta >20%
Mismatch between Console validation and runtime schema could block deployments; add pre-flight schema check in save flow
Complex UIs can increase cognitive load for non-technical users; add a simplified template mode for common patterns
implementation_plan: Week 1: Finalize mocks and handoff to eng; design to produce component library tokens and accessibility notes (owner: DES-2301)
Week 2: ENG to implement policy schema changes and validation service endpoint (owner: ENG-72415)
Week 3: Console UI implementation of Fanout editor and Preview simulator with local synthetic runs
Week 4: Integrate fallback suggestion API, test e2e in staging, and run customer-facing pilot with two beta customers
Week 5: Iterate on feedback, performance testing, and launch readiness checklist
testing_and_validation: Unit tests for validation logic (weight sums, exclusivity rules)
Integration tests for policy-to-runtime propagation using a sandboxed Smart Router instance
Usability test sessions with three customers from different segments (startup, mid-market, enterprise)
Performance tests for the preview simulator under 1000 concurrent preview requests
migration_notes: Existing simple region rules will be auto-migrated into single-target Fanout policies with 100% weight
Notify customers about minor semantic changes to fallback selection: explicit variant affinity will now override region-only rules
Provide a one-click 'legacy to fanout' conversion in the UI and record conversion audits
open_questions: Should probabilistic fanout be allowed on streaming sessions or limited to request-scoped routing? (awaiting ENG input)
What guardrails do we need for simultaneous canary and fanout policies to avoid exponential traffic duplication?
Do we support per-key deterministic pinning out-of-the-box or via an extension?
